358266.title: Connected sum formula for ECH spectral invariants
358266.statement:
Let $(Y_1,lambda_1)$ and $(Y_2,lambda_2)$ be closed connected contact three-manifolds with nonzero contact invariants, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. Write $(Y_1\#_{R}Y_2,\lambda_1\#_{R}\lambda_2)$ for their connected sum with parameter $R$, and let $c_k$ denote the $k$-th ECH spectral invariant. **Connected sum conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{R\to 0}c_k((Y_1\#_{R}Y_2,\lambda_1\#_{R}\lambda_2))=\max\{c_i(Y_1,\lambda_1)+c_j(Y_2,\lambda_2)\mid i+j=k\}.
$$

This conjecture predicts a max-convolution formula for ECH spectral invariants under connected sum, refining the connected sum computation of ECH at the module level. The statement is presented as a direction for future work, and its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

358789.title: Algebraic matroid basis conjecture for Grassmannians and coherent matching fields
358789.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Gr}(k,n)$ be the Grassmannian, and let $M_{\operatorname{Gr}(k,n)}$ be its algebraic matroid. For a coherent matching field $L$, let $M_L$ be the algebraic matroid realised by the linear span of the relevant Gröbner-fan cone. **Algebraic matroid basis conjecture.** Every basis of the algebraic matroid of the Grassmannian is a basis of $M_L$ for some coherent matching field $L$, i.e.,

$$
\mathcal B(M_{\operatorname{Gr}(k,n)})=\bigcup_{L\text{ coherent}}\mathcal B(M_L).
$$

The inclusion from each matching-field matroid into the Grassmannian matroid is known; the conjecture asserts the reverse inclusion. It is motivated by computations in all small examples considered, while non-matching-field cones of the tropical Grassmannian show that the claim is not immediate.

358810.title: The parity-dependent spectrum conjecture for repeated-part type-A seaweeds
358810.statement:
For integers $k,r\geq 1$, let

$$
\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{p}^A\frac{\overbrace{2k|\cdots|2k}^r|1}{2kr+1}.
$$

**Parity-dependent spectrum conjecture.** The seaweed $\mathfrak{g}$ is Frobenius, and the set of distinct eigenvalues in its spectrum is the collection of integers in

$$
\begin{cases}
[-2k+1,2k], & \text{if } r \text{ is odd};\\
[-k,k+1], & \text{if } r \text{ is even}.
\end{cases}
$$

Moreover, $\mathfrak{g}$ has the unimodal spectrum property. This conjecture records a further stable family of spectra; the paper gives related computations and notes that the family need not have the log-concave spectrum property, while the stated general assertion remains open.

358812.title: The log-concave spectrum conjecture for Frobenius maximal parabolic type-A seaweeds
358812.statement: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a Frobenius maximal parabolic type-A seaweed, meaning a Frobenius seaweed subalgebra of $\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ obtained from a maximal parabolic construction. Its spectrum is the multiset of eigenvalues of the adjoint action of a principal element, with multiplicities. **Log-concave spectrum conjecture.** The spectrum of $\mathfrak{g}$ has the log-concave spectrum property. The paper observes that log-concavity fails for Frobenius type-A seaweeds in general, but computations for maximal parabolic families suggest the stated restriction may force it; the conjecture remains open.

358821.title: The restricted amended Loneliness Spectrum Conjecture for four speeds
358821.statement:
Let $v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4$ be positive integers, and let

$$
\operatorname{ML}(v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4)=\max_{t\in\mathbb{R}}\min_{1\leq i\leq 4}\lVert tv_i\rVert,
$$

where $\lVert x\rVert$ denotes the absolute distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. **The restricted amended Loneliness Spectrum Conjecture.** One has either

$$
\exists s,k\in\mathbb{N},\quad k\in\{1,2\},\quad \operatorname{ML}(v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4)=\frac{s}{4s+k},
$$

or

$$
\operatorname{ML}(v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4)=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

The claim is motivated by computational evidence for four speeds: values with $k\notin\{1,2\}$ were not found below the stated bound. The source presents it as a further conjecture, without a general proof.

358922.title: Dyadic congruence conjecture for 2-regular partitions with designated summands
358922.statement:
Let $PD_2(n)$ denote the number of $2$-regular partitions of $n$ with designated summands, that is, partitions into odd parts with exactly one occurrence of each distinct part designated. For integers $k\geq 0$ and $n\geq 0$, **Dyadic congruence conjecture.**

$$
PD_2(2^{k+2}n)\equiv PD_2(2^kn)\pmod{2^{k+1}}.
$$

This proposed infinite family would extend the paper's internal congruences to all dyadic indices and modulus powers. The source reports only computational evidence and does not state that the conjecture has been proved or disproved.

358947.title: Spectral extension property for unitizations of semisimple Banach algebras
358947.statement:
Let $(A,\|\cdot\|)$ be a non-unital, semisimple Banach algebra, and let $A_e$ denote its unitization. Say that $A$ has the spectral extension property (SEP) when every norm on $A$ with the relevant spectral-extension property also has it after passing to the unitization. **Spectral extension conjecture.** If $A$ has SEP, then $A_e$ has SEP for semisimple Banach algebras.

This conjecture concerns whether SEP is preserved by unitization in the semisimple case. The paper's main theorem gives equivalent conditions characterizing this preservation, but the supplied text does not establish the conjecture independently; its resolution should therefore be checked against the theorem and its hypotheses.

358968.title: The planted dense subgraph recovery conjecture
358968.statement:
Let $G_n\sim\mathsf{PDS}(n,k_n,p_n,q_n)$, where the planted support has size $k_n$. Exact recovery means outputting the planted support. If $k_n=\omega(\sqrt n)$ and

$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\log_n\frac{k_n^2(p_n-q_n)^2}{nq_n(1-q_n)}<0,
$$

**the planted dense subgraph recovery conjecture.** No polynomial-time algorithm $\mathcal{A}:G\to{[n]\choose k_n}$ can achieve exact recovery asymptotically.

The conjecture concerns the computational threshold for recovering the planted dense subgraph, which is asserted to be substantially stronger than the threshold for detection. The surrounding discussion attributes this conjectured threshold to prior work, but the supplied text gives no resolution.

359121.title: Extension of the refined convergence-rate bound to regular graphs
359121.statement:
Let the simple symmetric case mean the setting in which the relevant communication graph is regular but not necessarily transitive. Let the bound referred to in Theorem be the convergence-rate bound established there.

**Regular-graph extension conjecture.** The bound given in Theorem remains valid in the simple symmetric case, for example for regular graphs without transitivity.

This conjecture arose from numerical experiments suggesting that the refined bound also applies beyond transitive graphs. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source context.

359261.title: Three-move outcome segmentation conjecture
359261.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite two-dimensional vector subtraction ruleset, and let $|S|$ denote its size. An **outcome segmentation** is a finite union of outcome segments, where each outcome segment is a geometric region with a distinct regular pattern of outcomes.

**Three-move segmentation conjecture.** If $|S|=3$, there is an outcome segmentation.

The conjecture is motivated by computational experiments showing segmentation for many three-move rulesets. The source presents it among open problems and gives no proof or resolution status.

359278.title: Quadratic-bound reconstruction conjecture for tableau minors
359278.statement: Let $k\geq 2$ and let $T\in\operatorname{YT}(n)$, where $n\geq k^2+2k$. Here $\operatorname{M}_k(T)$ denotes the collection of $k$-minors of the standard Young tableau $T$. **Reconstruction conjecture.** The collection $\operatorname{M}_k(T)$ determines $T$. The quadratic bound is suggested by the cases checked by computer, and the conjecture concerns reconstructibility from $\operatorname{M}_k(T)$ for general $k$.

359279.title: Linear-bound multiset reconstruction conjecture for tableau minors
359279.statement: Let $k\geq 1$ and let $T\in\operatorname{YT}(n)$, where $n\geq k+4$. Here $\operatorname{mM}_k(T)$ denotes the multiset of $k$-minors of the standard Young tableau $T$. **Multiset reconstruction conjecture.** The multiset $\operatorname{mM}_k(T)$ determines $T$. This proposed linear bound is supported by computer verification for $k\leq 5$, and concerns reconstructibility from multisets of $k$-minors.

359324.title: Structural conjecture for near-extremal joints configurations
359324.statement: Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field, and let $(\mathcal{J},\mathcal{L})$ be a joints configuration in $\mathbb{F}^d$, with $J=|\mathcal{J}|$ joints and $L=|\mathcal{L}|$ lines. Assume that, for some $x\geq d$, $J=(1-o(1))\binom{x}{d}$ and $L=\binom{x}{d-1}$. Let the structural property in Lemma Structural be the property referred to in the source. **Structural conjecture.** There exists a subset $\mathcal{J}'\subseteq\mathcal{J}$ with $|\mathcal{J}'|=(1-o(1))J$ satisfying that structural property with $\mathcal{L}$. The conjecture predicts that asymptotically optimal configurations retain the expected combinatorial structure after discarding a negligible proportion of joints; the supplied excerpt does not state the content of Lemma Structural, so that detail remains to be verified.

359380.title: Complete-digraph edge-reversal conjecture for Jacobian matroids
359380.statement: Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be complete digraphs on $p$ nodes, with all edge directions agreeing except for the edge between nodes $p-1$ and $p$. **Complete-digraph edge-reversal conjecture.** The two graphs have the same Jacobian matroid. The conjecture concerns a limitation of Jacobian-matroid methods: even complete graphs differing only by this edge orientation may define the same matroid. The paper reports computational evidence for related coincidences but gives no proof or resolution of this claim.

359425.title: Interlacing conjecture for deformed monotone Hurwitz numbers
359425.statement:
Let $g\geqslant 0$, $n\geqslant 1$, and let $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_n\geqslant 1$. The **deformed monotone Hurwitz number** $\vec{H}^t_{g,n}(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_n)$ is a polynomial in $t$. Two real-rooted polynomials interlace when their roots weakly alternate, with their degrees differing by one. **Interlacing conjecture.** The polynomial $\vec{H}^t_{g,n}(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_n)$ interlaces each of the $n$ polynomials 
$$
\vec{H}^t_{g,n}(\mu_1+1,\mu_2,\ldots,\mu_n),\quad \vec{H}^t_{g,n}(\mu_1,\mu_2+1,\ldots,\mu_n),\quad\ldots,\quad \vec{H}^t_{g,n}(\mu_1,\mu_2,\ldots,\mu_n+1).
$$
 For fixed $(g,n)$ this predicts a lattice of interlacing polynomials; it has been checked computationally in many cases, but remains unproved in general.

359582.title: The height-two poset linear-extension almost-completeness conjecture
359582.statement: Let $e(P)$ be the number of linear extensions of a finite poset $P$, and let $e'$ denote its restriction to posets of height two. Write $\mathcal T_{e'}$ for the set of values attained by $e'$. **Height-two linear-extension conjecture.** The function $e'$ is almost complete, meaning that its value set contains all but finitely many positive integers. Numerical evidence exhibits many missing values, but height-two posets have sufficiently many possible inputs and the restricted function can attain large primes, so the conjecture remains plausible and open.

359589.title: The concise tree-counting conjecture for planar graphs
359589.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a simple planar graph, and let $tr(G)$ be the number of trees in $G$ of all sizes. **Planar tree-counting conjecture.** The function $tr$ is concise: every positive integer should be realized by a planar graph whose size is bounded by a fixed polynomial in the logarithm of that integer. The function is already almost complete because an empty graph on $n$ vertices has $n$ trees, and its computation is $\#\mathrm P$-complete, but conciseness remains open.

359636.title: Triangle-free Cohen–Macaulay oriented graph conjecture
359636.statement: Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ be a weighted oriented graph whose underlying graph $G$ is **triangle-free**, meaning that $G$ contains no cycles of length $3$. The graph $G$ is Cohen–Macaulay when its edge ideal is Cohen–Macaulay, and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ is unmixed when all of its minimal vertex covers have the same cardinality. **Triangle-free Cohen–Macaulay oriented graph conjecture.** $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if $G$ is Cohen–Macaulay and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ is unmixed. This is proposed based on the preceding theorem and the authors' computations; its status remains open in the source.

359740.title: The prime-order even-list conjecture for perfect matchings
359740.statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $K_{2p}$ be the complete graph on $2p$ circularly ordered vertices, and let $L$ be a list of $p$ positive integers less than $p$. A perfect matching $F$ of $K_{2p}$ is a set of $p$ pairwise disjoint edges covering all vertices, and $\ell(F)$ denotes its list of edge-lengths. **Prime-order even-list conjecture.** There exists a perfect matching $F$ of $K_{2p}$ such that $\ell(F)=L$ if and only if the number of even integers in $L$ is even. This addresses the even case of the seating couple problem under the stronger assumption that the number of couples is an odd prime. The paper presents it as an open conjecture motivated by necessary conditions and computational evidence.

359753.title: The Gamma-bound dominance conjecture for integer D-optimality
359753.statement:
Let $s$ and $q$ be the parameters defining the feasible bounds in the integer D-optimality formulation, and let $\mathfrak{z}_{\text{tiny $\Gamma$}}$ and $\mathfrak{z}_{\text{tiny $\mathcal{H}$}}$ denote the corresponding objective bounds.

**Gamma-bound dominance conjecture.** For $s-q\geq 1$, we have

$$
\mathfrak{z}_{\text{\tiny $\Gamma$}}\leq \mathfrak{z}_{\text{\tiny $\mathcal{H}$}}.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by numerical experiments: equality is observed when $s=1$, while strict inequality is always observed when $s>1$. The paper presents this as a conjecture based on those experiments; no proof or resolution is supplied.
